script.title: sqrt-impact-law-explainer

story_plan.cold_open_logic: Everyone has seen a price move when someone buys a lot of something — this hook makes that physical and immediate before any crypto context appears.

script.hook: Buy a little, the price barely moves. Buy a lot, and the price jumps — but not as much as you'd expect.

segments.voiceover: Buy a little, the price barely moves. Buy a lot, and the price jumps, but not as much as you'd expect.

display.line: More buying = higher price. But how much higher?

segments.voiceover: Think of it like scooping water from a pool. The first scoop is easy. Each scoop after gets harder. You're always pulling, but the pool never drains at the same rate.

Markets work the same way. Double the buying pressure, and the price doesn't double, it follows a square-root curve. It rises, but slower and slower. This is called the square-root impact law. It's how traders actually model price movement.

display.annotation: Price impact grows — but flattens as volume rises

segments.voiceover: The published framework plugs real numbers into this law: two billion dollars in daily flow, a float of twenty-five billion XRP. The math produces a derived anchor from published inputs, five hundred and eighty-nine dollars. Not a promise. A calculation you can check yourself at xrpvaluation.info.
